steps.intro: Nouns change their endings too. Watch the endings of the nouns: they show who does what, wherever the word stands.

cards.en: The servant sees the master. (same meaning: the endings decide, not the order)

cards.title: Subject and object endings
body: The doer of the verb (the subject) takes one set of endings; the thing the verb is done to (the object) takes another. Grammar books call these the nominative and accusative cases.
λόγος, ἀδελφός, κύριος and many other nouns ending -ος follow this pattern (the second declension).

cards.title: “The” changes too
body: The article (“the”) has the same jobs: ὁ and οἱ with subjects, τόν and τούς with objects. Greek has no word for “a”: λόγος alone is “a word”.
Because endings carry the meaning, Greek can put words in almost any order. Find the verb, then find its subject (-ος, -οι) and its object (-ον, -ους).
The verb agrees with its subject: one brother λέγει, more than one λέγουσιν.

cards.title: How dictionaries list nouns
body: A noun is listed in its subject form, one of it: λόγος. Word lists often add the article to show its gender: ὁ λόγος means a masculine noun. These words are masculine because of how the language works, not because of what they mean: ὁ νόμος, the law, is masculine too.

cards.prompt: ὁ ἄνθρωπος βλέπει τὸν ἀδελφόν. Who sees whom?
cards.explain: ἄνθρωπος (-ος) is the subject; ἀδελφόν (-ον) is the object.

cards.prompt: τὸν ἀδελφὸν βλέπει ὁ ἄνθρωπος. Now who sees whom?
cards.explain: The order changed, but the endings didn't: ὁ ἄνθρωπος is still the subject and τὸν ἀδελφόν the object.

cards.prompt: Match each ending to its job.

cards.explain: -ους is the object ending for more than one: “words”, as the object of the verb.
-οι is the subject ending for more than one: “brothers” doing the action.

cards.prompt: Which verb fits? οἱ δοῦλοι ___ τὸν κύριον (the servants see the master).
cards.explain: οἱ δοῦλοι is “they” (more than one), so the verb takes -ουσιν.

cards.prompt: Write “The brothers hear the law”, in the same order as the English.
cards.explain: οἱ ἀδελφοὶ (subject) ἀκούουσιν (they hear) τὸν νόμον (object).

steps.intro: Find the verb, then its subject (-ος, -οι) and its object (-ον, -ους).

cards.note: ὁ θεὸς is the subject, τὸν υἱὸν the object: “For God did not send his Son into the world to condemn the world…”
οἱ λόγοι μου, “my words”, is a subject with -οι: “Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.”
